A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GeN optimization work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic optimization and vision/language experiments in Sections 5–6, plus image-generation and recommendation results in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds CIFAR10 training-from-scratch results in Appendix C.6 and Figure 15.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 now updates the learning rate only when fitted coefficients A* and b* are positive. The core GeN update and multipoint fitting already existed; Algorithm 2 formalizes the Hessian-vector computation route previously discussed in Section 3.2.

E1.justification: Dataset and task coverage is retained. Appendix C.6 adds training from scratch on the existing CIFAR10 classification task, changing training initialization and procedure rather than the represented data or task requirements.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in retained experiments is unchanged. Figure 15 uses already evaluated methods: cosine-decay AdamW, Prodigy and D-adaptation with AdamW. Newly discussed LQA, QLABGrad and ADLER are not experimentally compared.

E3.justification: Appendix C.6 introduces 15-epoch ResNet18 training from scratch with AdamW at 1e-3 and GeN frequency 4. Figure 2 adds R² evaluation of quadratic fits. Appendix B.1 corrects the learning-rate search exponent range from k=-5,...,0 to k=5,4,...,0; this does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Figure 2 strengthens the existing quadratic-approximation diagnostic with quantitative goodness-of-fit values. Existing batch-size, model-size, update-frequency and initial-learning-rate sensitivity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting remains unchanged, including the identical ± entries in Table 5. No new seed counts, repeated-run information, confidence intervals or significance tests are supplied. The added R² values measure fit quality.

E6.justification: Figure 15 adds training-from-scratch convergence results showing similar final accuracy across GeN and its comparators. Figure 2 newly reports R² values of 0.994, 0.998, 0.997 and 0.999. Existing benchmark values in Tables 2–5 and 7 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: New Appendix E introduces Theorem 1 and a proof claiming local quadratic convergence of exact GeN-GD under convexity, Lipschitz and derivative conditions. Appendix A.5 adds explicit fitting and five-point derivations, while A.3 corrects the curvature numerator from -L0 to +L0. The convergence theorem substantially expands the theoretical scope.

C1.justification: The introduction removes the claim that GeN is the first automatic optimizer applicable to general optimizers. The abstract and conclusion retain the main claims concerning automatic learning rates, general applicability, efficiency and empirical performance.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly distinguishes approximate Algorithm 1 from exact GeN and emphasizes quadratic-fit validation in Appendix D.4. Appendix A.5 adds the interpretation that more fitting points yield slightly steadier convergence and similar accuracy at greater cost. Existing large-batch recommendations and the global-convergence caveat remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds higher-order differentiation pseudocode, names the five Mask R-CNN losses, and supplies settings and a source reference for the new training-from-scratch experiment. It removes the abstract's promised AutoGeN code-release link; actual repository availability cannot be determined from the PDFs.

R1.justification: New Appendices D.3–D.4 substantially expand second-order optimization background and comparisons with LQA, QLABGrad and ADLER. v2 acknowledges GeN-SGD's equivalence to LQA and positions its contribution around general preconditioning, flexible fitting and practical refinements, materially revising novelty attribution.

P1.justification: The title drops Automatic, an equal-contribution note is added, and Section 3.3 is rewritten around explicit curve fitting and its relationship to LQA. Several appendix subsections are added, but the overall section sequence and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 15 and Algorithm 2, expands Algorithm 1, revises Figure 1's line styles and legends, annotates Figure 2 with R², simplifies Figure 8's legends and clarifies Figure 11's caption. Existing tables and most figure content are preserved, with some relocation.

improvement.justification: v2 improves prior-work attribution, corrects a finite-difference formula and adds quantitative fit checks and training-from-scratch evidence. However, Appendix E's new convergence proof drops the error component outside the generalized inverse's rank-one projection, leaving its quadratic-convergence guarantee unsupported. These benefits coexist with a substantive new theoretical defect, making the net quality change uncertain.
